# T005 — Repair backend HTTP dependency advisories

## Summary

Updated the backend HTTP family on Express **4**, with the patched transitive packages resolved in both npm lockfiles. Fresh npm audits changed from root **56** / standalone backend **18** affected package entries to root **51** / backend **13**. Both post-change audits have no vulnerable Express, body-parser, proxy-addr, path-to-regexp or qs entries. These counts represent affected packages, not distinct advisories.

## Changes

- `backend/package.json`: raise the existing direct Express constraint from `^4.18.2` to `^4.22.3` and body-parser from `^1.20.2` to `^1.20.8`; preserve Express 4 and the existing API.
- `package-lock.json`: npm 11 workspace install resolves Express 4.22.3, body-parser 1.20.8, proxy-addr 2.0.8, path-to-regexp 0.1.13 and qs 6.16.1. npm hoisted the prior backend-local HTTP tree to root; npm also adjusted a few shared side-channel metadata/patch entries. No manual lock edits or unrelated direct dependency changes.
- `backend/package-lock.json`: npm standalone lock resolution installs the same patched HTTP versions (including proxy-addr via `npm update proxy-addr --package-lock-only --workspaces=false`). npm updated nearby transitive patches/placement; no new direct dependencies.

## Decisions

Fresh scans: `npm audit --json` against **both** lockfiles, 2026-10-20, npm 11.19.0 / Node 24.21.0. Verified package ranges and first patched versions with the [GitHub Advisory Database API](https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h) and the linked per-advisory records. `npm explain cookie` identified the remaining root cookie 0.5.0 under frontend `@azure/static-web-apps-cli`, **not** Express; changing that delivery-tool family is outside T005 (T008).

| Advisory | Severity | Package | From → to (both locks) | Direct / transitive, parent | Status and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h) | Critical | proxy-addr | 2.0.7 → 2.0.8 | Transitive, Express; patched at 2.0.8 | Fixed; `req.ip` spoofing requires misconfigured trusted IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnet; no `trust proxy` configuration found in backend source. |
| [GHSA-37ch-88jc-xwx2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-37ch-88jc-xwx2) | High | path-to-regexp | 0.1.12 → 0.1.13 | Transitive, Express; patched at 0.1.13 | Fixed; denial of service requires attacker-influenced route definition with multiple params, not observed in existing static backend routes. |
| [GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6) | Low | body-parser | 1.20.3 → 1.20.8 | Direct and Express transitive; patched at 1.20.6 | Fixed; backend uses `bodyParser.json()` and `.text()` with default limits, not an invalid configured limit. |
| [GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), [GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p), [GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26), [GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) | Low / moderate | qs | 6.13.0 → 6.16.1 | Transitive, body-parser / Express; respective first patches 6.14.2, 6.14.1, 6.15.2, 6.16.0 | Fixed; query parsing is HTTP-exposed; the documented `parse` → `stringify` with `plainObjects` / `allowPrototypes` is not found in backend source. |
| [GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x) | Low | cookie (Express copy) | 0.7.1 → 0.7.1 (already patched) | Transitive, Express; patched at 0.7.0 | Already fixed in Express graph; **separate root cookie 0.5.0 remains open** through frontend delivery tool, T008. |

Express 4.21.2 → 4.22.3 is the same-major parent upgrade resolving its derived high audit entry; body-parser and qs also contributed derived moderate entries. No Express 5 migration or blanket override was used.

## Follow-ups and risks

- **Open, not accepted or suppressed:** remaining root 51 and backend 13 affected package entries include the Azure SDK/Speech/XML family, frontend Vite/lint and SWA delivery-tool families, backend nodemon and other transitive tooling. Owners must triage these in T006–T008 and the final report; the root cookie 0.5.0 is a SWA CLI dependency, not an HTTP-server exception. Scanner reports enumerate every remaining entry; no finding was silently declared safe and no owner acceptance has been obtained.
- The task's offline route characterization cannot validate deployed proxy configuration or live ACS; verify actual trust-proxy settings and deployment after change. Request high-risk code review at the phase boundary. The checkpoint runner may default to Node 22 unless configured for Node 24; our commands explicitly selected Node 24 but cannot control its environment.
